own_solution.law: Using K = p²/(2m) and λ = h/p gives λ = hc/√(2mc²K). Convert mc² to 511000 eV and the resulting wavelength from nm to pm.
assumptions: The electron starts from rest and is treated nonrelativistically, as stated.
The other apparatus has no specified interaction with the electron.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: TD0E0 and T3B16 omit the 90 eV specified in their quantified twins, violating the review requirement that variants of the same quantity preserve its number and unit.

counterexamples: TD0E0 permits an additional alpha-particle kinetic energy of 10 eV, whereas its quantified twin TCF3D specifies 90 eV.
T3B16 permits an additional proton kinetic energy of 10 eV, whereas its quantified twin TF42A specifies 90 eV.
notes: All physical classifications and certified answers are correct. For electron energy increments of 40, 90 and 180 eV, the wavelengths are respectively 88.9855, 79.1755 and 67.5211 pm. The other-apparatus additions leave the wavelength at 100.15 pm. All energies remain comfortably nonrelativistic. The explicitly claimed minimal_pair_with pairs preserve 90 eV and change the physical attachment appropriately. Pass 2 explains that the two unquantified sentences are intentional numeral-free controls; nevertheless, the supplied review instructions provide no exception to their number-and-unit preservation requirement, so the pass-1 rendering defect remains. The pass-1 answers in nm agree with the packet's answers in pm after conversion.
